result.title: Channel Match: Calibrating Shape Latents for Few-Step 3D Generation
result.summary: Recent native 3D generators achieve high-quality asset creation by modeling structured 3D latents with flow-based transformers, but their high-resolution generation remains computationally expensive due to costly iterative sampling. In this work, we introduce a few-step distillation framework for native 3D generation, enabled by continuous self-consistency training with a custom JVP FlashAttention kernel and an analytic velocity regression objective for sparse structured 3D latents. To stabilize joint optimization, we further introduce an adaptive loss weighting strategy that automatically balances them without manual tuning. Beyond acceleration, we reveal a previously overlooked failure mode of few-step native 3D generation: sampling-induced latent distribution drift preserves geometric correctness but disrupts downstream PBR texture synthesis, causing texture artifacts on geometrically valid assets. To address this issue, we propose Channel Match, a training-free adaptive per-channel latent calibration method that restores the latent distribution without modifying either generator. We validate our approach on TRELLIS.2 at the $1024^3$ resolution setting. Our two-step model achieves $4.5\times$ faster geometry sampling while maintaining geometry quality comparable to the many-step teacher, and Channel Match further improves rendering quality by recovering the latent interface between geometry and appearance generation.

AI.brief_summary: 面向原生 3D 生成，提出基于连续自一致性训练与解析速度回归的少步蒸馏框架以加速高分辨率采样，并揭示采样引起的 latent 分布漂移虽保持几何正确却破坏 PBR 纹理生成，进而提出免训练、逐通道自适应的 latent 校准方法 Channel Match。
AI.relevance_reason: 虽属 3D 资产生成而非 VLM 推理，但其「采样导致的 latent 分布漂移」诊断与免训练逐通道校准思路，可能可供核查 latent 推理状态的分布漂移、通道结构及对下游使用的影响。
